deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematical derivation. It is the first page of a cover letter dated 'Kerstlingerode bei Göttingen, den 9. Septbr 1875', nine years after Riemann's death, so it is not by Riemann. The writer is almost certainly Karl Hattendorff, who worked up Riemann's posthumous paper 'Über die Fläche vom kleinsten Inhalt bei gegebener Begrenzung' (Abh. Ges. Wiss. Göttingen 13, 1867). The addressee ('Geehrtester Herr College') is very probably Heinrich Weber, who was then editing Riemann's Gesammelte Werke (1876) together with Dedekind.

The writer sends a revised version ('neue Bearbeitung') of the minimal-surface treatise for the collected works. He says he has carefully used the addressee's comments and then adds remarks on details, beginning with notation.

(1) Partial derivatives were not written with the round ∂ in the first printing (1867). The reason was that the printer did not own that type and would not acquire it.

(2) The term 'Argument' for the coefficient of i in the logarithm of a complex quantity goes back to Riemann himself. In modern terms, log w = log|w| + i arg w. Riemann reportedly used this word, and no other, in his lectures and in his oral explanations to the writer about the manuscript. The writer therefore asks, on the next page, that the term be kept.

Context:
- The previous folio is part of Hattendorff's worked-out text. It covers the example of a minimal surface bounded by two circles in parallel planes, where x and m are elliptic integrals in q.
- The next page continues the letter. It discusses the historical introduction, including Poisson's note on the Plateau problem.

The only mathematical content here is the definition arg w = Im(log w), which is implicit in the remark.
errors: No mathematical errors; the page is editorial correspondence. Attribution caveat: the folio sits in the Riemann bundle but is not by Riemann. It is a post-1866 letter, very probably from Hattendorff, concerning the edition of Riemann's minimal-surface paper for the 1876 Werke.

results.what: Editorial note: the round ∂ was absent from the 1867 printing of Riemann's minimal-surface paper because the printer lacked the type.
results.modern_name: Typographical/editorial history of Riemann's 'Fläche vom kleinsten Inhalt'
results.usually_credited_to: Hattendorff (editor, 1867); Weber/Dedekind edition of Riemann's Werke (1876)

results.what: Claim that the term 'Argument' for Im(log w), the angle of a complex number, was Riemann's own usage in lectures and in his explanations of the manuscript.
results.modern_name: Argument of a complex number, arg w = Im log w
results.usually_credited_to: The term is commonly traced to Cauchy (and, as a concept, to Argand and others) in the first half of the 19th century

deep.surprise_reason: The page is an 1875 editorial letter (probably Hattendorff to Weber), not Riemann's mathematics. It holds only minor historical anecdotes: the printer lacked a ∂ type, and Riemann used the word 'Argument'. These are of mild interest for the edition history of the Werke but contain no new mathematical result.

transcription_corrections: Transcription is essentially correct. Small points: in 'Abhandlung' the writer has overwritten/corrected the first letters ('Ab'). The '4' in the right margin near the salutation is a later foliation/page mark, not part of the text.
